title: GPU utilization anomaly investigation - na clusters - march 2026
body:
GPU Utilization anomaly - North America clusters (investigation notes)

Summary:
- Between 2026-03-19 22:00 and 2026-03-20 03:30 UTC we observed sustained elevated GPU utilization across three NA clusters (na-cluster-7, na-cluster-11, na-cluster-14) with sudden drops in headroom on pool:dedicated-a and pool:ephemeral-ml-b. Peak per-cluster GPU utilization reached 87% (3h moving average) on na-cluster-11 at 2026-03-20 01:12 UTC.
- This doc is an export of dashboard panels, ad-hoc queries, hypotheses, and short-term mitigation proposals for capacity planning and follow-ups.

Key metrics / snapshots (derived from Grafana panels and Prometheus queries):
- na-cluster-11: 3h avg util = 87%, 95th pct instantaneous = 94%, free-gpu-sockets = 6 (down from baseline 42)
- na-cluster-7: 3h avg util = 72%, sustained at ~70% for 5 hours
- na-cluster-14: 3h avg util = 64%, spike coincident with scheduled batch job window (00:45-02:00 UTC)
- pool:dedicated-a (multi-tenant reserved): cluster-weighted util = 83%, variance across nodes high (stdev 12pp)
- pool:ephemeral-ml-b (spot style / burst): observed eviction churn + queue backlog growth (queued requests +120% vs baseline)
- overall NA region headroom dropped from 28% -> 9% (24h baseline comparison)

Timeline of notable events:
- 2026-03-19 20:30 UTC: Routine overnight batch rollout started (deploy batch-model-v3 across infra projects) — recorded in deploy log (linked in JIRA-OPS-1248).
- 2026-03-19 21:05 UTC: Autoscaler config for pool:ephemeral-ml-b was changed (scale_down_grace_seconds lowered from 300 to 60) — PR #872.
- 2026-03-19 22:05 UTC: Monitoring alerted: region_gpu_headroom < 12% — alert routed to #infra-alerts.
- 2026-03-20 00:50 UTC: na-cluster-11 shows memory pressure events coincident with long-running KV-cache misses (observed via runtime tracing).
- 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC: Temporary mitigation (scale up + provision 8 gpus to na-cluster-11) applied; headroom restored to ~23% by 02:45 UTC.

Ad-hoc queries used (Prometheus / BigQuery style):
- prom: sum(rate(gpu_utilization_seconds_total[5m])) by (cluster) / count(node_gpu_sockets_total{cluster})
- prom: topk(10, sum(gpu_utilization_seconds_total) by (pool, cluster))
- bq: SELECT cluster, pool, AVG(util_pct) FROM gpu_daily_metrics WHERE date BETWEEN '2026-03-15' AND '2026-03-20' GROUP BY cluster, pool
- grafana panel link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/cluster-utilization/na-gpu-overview?panelId=7

Per-cluster observations and hypotheses:
- na-cluster-11:
  - Observation: Highest sustained util, high variance, multiple long-running sessions pinned to few GPUs (a small number of jobs consuming >40% of a GPU for hours).
  - Hypotheses: 1) A rollout caused old long-tail batch jobs to re-run without queue sharding; 2) KV cache misses forced model contexts to regen, increasing token compute; 3) Noise from a single tenant running aggressive eval tests.
  - Evidence: Traces show repeated model reloads (runtime logs) and one job id (job-8893) shows repeated restarts.

- na-cluster-7:
  - Observation: Elevated baseline but no extreme variance; distribution suggests many smaller sessions rather than a single offender.
  - Hypotheses: Traffic shift (small customers) + autoscaler thresholds too conservative for short bursts.

- na-cluster-14:
  - Observation: Spike window aligned to scheduled nightly batch (00:45-02:00 UTC). Pool eviction queue grew 30% during that window.
  - Hypotheses: Nightly batch sizing too large relative to pool capacity; batch jobs not using local cache warming; scheduled concurrently with canary experiments.

Pool-level notes (dedicated-a, ephemeral-ml-b, shared-inference):
- dedicated-a: high utilization with hot nodes — imbalance likely due to placement affinity (customer pinning) and insufficient redistribution logic. Suggest: run a rebalance job to shuffle low-priority workloads to clusters with spare capacity.
- ephemeral-ml-b: autoscaler config change on 2026-03-19 likely reduced effective headroom by shortening scale-down; coupled with eviction churn this amplified queuing. Suggest: revert scale_down_grace_seconds to 300 for this pool and monitor.
- shared-inference: unaffected, baseline steady at 21% util. Good candidate to borrow one node temporarily if needed.

Immediate actions taken (short-term mitigations):
- +8 GPUs added to na-cluster-11 (manual provisioning) at 2026-03-20 01:58 UTC — reduced immediate pressure. Owner: Ethan Park.
- Rolled back autoscaler change for ephemeral-ml-b at 2026-03-20 03:05 UTC (PR #879). Owner: Ava Chen.
- Added temporary alert rule to flag pool imbalance when node-level stdev(util) > 10pp for >15m.

Recommended follow-ups (capacity planning & longer term):
1) Capacity rebalancing runbook: schedule an automated rebalance to redistribute pinned workloads from dedicated-a hotspots to na-cluster-14 and shared-inference. Estimated impact: recover 6-10% headroom in dedicated-a. Owner: Priya Nambiar. ETA: 2026-03-25.
2) Autoscaler policy review: revert quick scale-down changes across ephemeral pools; add rate limit on scale events to avoid oscillation. Owner: Diego Morales. ETA: 2026-03-28.
3) Batch scheduling window evaluation: move non-critical nightly batches to staggered windows; add prewarm steps to avoid cold KV-cache penalties. Owner: Platform Scheduling. ETA: 2026-04-05.
4) Invest in per-tenant fairness throttles: protect reserved pools from noisy evaluations that can spike utilization. Product ticket: PRD-398 (link pending).
5) Add a daily capacity digest (dashboard panel) showing predicted 7-day headroom using job calendar and recent trend to inform Dedicated capacity commits. Owner: eng-infra analytics.

Notes for capacity planning models:
- Use median 95th-utilization baseline rather than mean to avoid being skewed by short spikes when planning reserved capacity.
- Model an 'eviction amplification factor' for ephemeral pools when average eviction rate > 5/hr — historical factor ~1.4x extra GPU time used because of retries.

Open questions / unresolved diagnostics:
- What caused job-8893 repeated restarts? Need to correlate with deploys and tenant logs.
- Are there any recent changes to model checkpoints that increase cold-start cost (larger weights, different quantization)? Check model-onboarding PRs in last 7 days.
- Can we get a per-tenant breakdown of GPU-hours for the offending window (privacy-safe aggregation)? Responsible: product-privacy + infra-analytics.

Attachments / snapshot exports included in this sheet (panels copied):
- Panel: NA region headroom timeseries (2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-22)
- Panel: Top 10 GPU consumers by job id (2026-03-20 window)
- Panel: Pool-level eviction vs queue size scatter (nightly)

Next steps and owners summary:
- Priya Nambiar: run rebalance plan and update capacity model assumptions. (ETA 2026-03-25)
- Diego Morales: autoscaler policy audit + rollback verification. (ETA 2026-03-28)
- Ethan Park: dig into job-8893 and storage / checkpoints. (ETA 2026-03-23)
- Ava Chen: monitor post-mitigation metrics and confirm headroom stable for 48h. (ETA 2026-03-22)

This sheet is a working export from the Grafana + Prometheus dashboards and internal BigQuery metrics. It is intentionally informal and meant to capture investigation artifacts for the capacity planning team. Please add notes inline or push follow-up tasks to JIRA-OPS-1248.

Raw snapshot (numeric excerpts):
- na-cluster-11: avg_gpu_util_3h=0.87, max_inst=0.94, free_sockets=6
- na-cluster-7: avg_gpu_util_3h=0.72, peak_inst=0.83
- region-na-headroom_before=0.28, region-na-headroom_after=0.23 (post-scale)

End of export.
